 Motor racing-Norris fastest in Mexico City practice ahead of Antonelli
 Sunday, 01 Nov 2026
 | 4:37 AM MYT
 share 
 bookmark 
 Formula One F1 - Mexico City Grand Prix - Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez, Mexico City, Mexico - October 31, 2026 McLaren's Lando Norris during practice REUTERS/Raquel Cunha 
 MEXICO CITY, Oct ⁠31 (Reuters) - Reigning champion Lando Norris was fastest on ⁠Saturday in final practice for a Mexico City ‌Grand Prix set to crown 20-year-old Mercedes driverKimi Antonelli as Formula One's youngest title winner.
 The McLaren driver put in a flying late lap ​of one minute 17.600 seconds at ⁠the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez ⁠to top thetimesheets by the slimmest of margins, 0.001 ⁠faster ‌than Antonelli who is poised to become Italy's first F1 world champion since 1953.
 Ferrari's CharlesLeclerc, ⁠fastest in both Friday sessions, was third quickest ​and 0.117 ‌off the pace, with McLaren's Oscar Piastri fourth.
 Red Bull's ⁠four-times champion ​Max Verstappen, who has a one place grid drop for Sunday's race, was fifth fastest ahead of Ferrari's seven-times ⁠champion Lewis Hamilton.
 George Russell, Antonelli's teammate ​and closest rival, was seventh.
 Russell is 123 points behind Antonelli and has to win on Sunday to prevent the Italian ⁠taking the title in Mexico. Antonelli will be champion if he finishes ninth or higher.
 Japan's RyoHirakawa, replacing Frenchman Esteban Ocon at Haas and set for his F1 ​debut at the age of 32, ⁠was 19th fastest.
 Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto and Cadillac's home hero ​Sergio Perez failed to set any ‌timed laps, with both having ​changes of their cars' power units ahead of qualifying.
 (Reporting by Alan Baldwin, editing by Ed Osmond)
